service.name: Live band karaoke
service.serviceType: Live band karaoke for company parties, after-parties and private events
service.description: A live band that plays 80s and 90s hits as a party band and hands the microphone to guests who want to sing, with lyrics on a screen and a host, for company holiday parties, sales kickoffs, after-parties and private events across Denver and Colorado.

faqs.a: No. The band plays a full set of 80s and 90s hits on its own, sung out front, and the night works as a party band night if nobody ever takes the mic. The host keeps the invitation open all night, and nobody is ever put on the spot.

faqs.q: What if nobody volunteers at first?
faqs.a: That’s the usual start, and it’s why the band opens with its own set rather than an empty stage. The host works the floor, the first singers are almost always a pair or a group, and the band covers the harmony and the high notes for whoever is up there. Once two or three songs have gone well, the list fills on its own.

faqs.q: How does a guest get on the list?
faqs.a: The songbook is printed for the tables. A guest picks a song, gives the host their name and the title, and the host keeps the list and calls each singer up. There’s no app and nothing to download.

faqs.q: How is this different from a karaoke DJ?
faqs.a: With a backing track the guest is on their own. With a band, the tempo follows the singer, the band vamps if somebody loses the verse, a second voice comes in on the chorus, and the song ends when it should rather than when the file does. The words are on a screen either way. What changes is who’s standing behind the singer.

faqs.q: How many people get a turn?
faqs.a: About six to ten guest songs fit in an hour. At a party of two hundred that means most people sing along from the floor rather than from the stage, which is how the night is meant to work. A long list is a reason to book the karaoke chapter longer, and there is no overtime rate if it runs on.

faqs.q: Can a group go up together?
faqs.a: Yes, and the first singers of the night nearly always do. Two or three colleagues on one song is the easiest way onto the list, and the band carries the harmony and the high notes for whoever is up there.
The person booking. Say when you book whether the songs run clean or as recorded, and the host keeps to it on the night.

The songbook runs from the 80s and 90s onward, the songs an office of mixed ages all know: Journey, Bon Jovi, Whitney Houston, Prince, Madonna, Queen, Oasis, No Doubt, Alanis Morissette, TLC, the Backstreet Boys, Outkast, the Killers. It is printed and on the screen, and a specific song for a specific person is a request we take before the night.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the act need?
faqs.a: The four-piece plays in 14 by 10 feet on two dedicated 20-amp circuits with a 90-minute load-in, plus a lyric screen facing the stage and one facing the crowd. Sound support that’s the right size for the venue is included, and an announcement microphone is ready for the remarks and a raffle.

faqs.q: Can the karaoke follow a dinner set?
faqs.a: Yes. The same band plays dinner at conversation volume, 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, and turns up when the program ends. One contract, one load-in, one sound system, and the karaoke set is planned with your run of show.
